source.pc: In this skill you learn to expand double brackets. If we multiply a sum within brackets by another sum within brackets, like in , you should be able to write this without brackets. In this example this results in . This skill also includes somewhat more complicated terms in the sums inside said brackets and/or larger sums with more terms.

We know how to expand brackets like . But what do we do if we have a multiplication of brackets with brackets? Like ? The answer is: we expand brackets twice. First we expand one, and then we expand the other.
If we have a number multiplication, like for instance , then we can visualize this multiplication using blocks.
From this, we see that can first be rewritten to and then to . Check for yourself: they all result into .
This works exactly the same if we have an expression like . Here, , , and can be any type of expression, like or anything similar. We can again visualize this.

From this visualization, we see that we may rewrite to . We call this expanding double brackets. The accompanying rule is You generally don't need to remember this rule. What you should remember is that you multiply each of the terms from the left brackets (here and ) with each of the terms from the right brackets (here and ). If you do this for all combinations of terms, you get the right result.
